title: A multi-agent LLM system for spatial transcriptomics nominates ICAM1 in lung fibrosis
summary: DeepMAST, a multi-agent system that runs spatial transcriptomics analysis on locally deployed large language models with a retrieval-augmented literature system and guardrails, nominated ICAM1 as a candidate therapeutic target in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. The abstract reports support from human-tissue immunostaining and ICAM-1 blockade in a preclinical fibrosis model, and better evidence retrieval and fewer unsupported interpretations than baseline conditions in benchmarks. ICAM-1 was already studied in fibrosis, and only the abstract was reviewed.
ai_technology: DeepMAST multi-agent LLM system with MCP-enabled spatial analysis tools and retrieval-augmented generation, prioritizing targets from Visium data

evidence.tested: Target nomination by DeepMAST was followed by human-tissue immunostaining and ICAM-1 blockade in a preclinical fibrosis model.
evidence.unknown: Whether ICAM-1 blockade has therapeutic benefit beyond the preclinical model; quantitative effect sizes, which the abstract does not give; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: LLM agents orchestrated the spatial transcriptomics analysis and nominated ICAM1 from curated evidence.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI. Publisher full text not accessed. Author affiliations from OpenAlex metadata.
